body.statement: For the exact four-relation transition system, can one prove that every irreducible residual token has a verifier-accepted candidate: either a projection circuit whose cross-multiplied target identity holds on \(\mathcal I_H\), or a signed canonical-row contrast whose rational box lifts through all interacting districts, fixed kernels, and observed descendants while preserving every supported observed cell and exactly \(H\)? The proof must also exclude an identified residual whose only identifying functional is nonrational.
body.justification: This is the genuine open content: local contextwise witnesses do not automatically couple across shared selector gates and interacting districts.
body.gap: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser explicitly conjecture completeness; Kivva and coauthors solve a different positivity-qualified gID reduction, and no searched paper supplies this fixed-support residual alternative.
body.consumer: Resolving the dichotomy yields a decision procedure that never invents an unsupplied experimental regime and explains every failure by an exact global pair.

obligation.what_is_open: An exhaustiveness theorem for the residual projection and signed-row-swap libraries on every reachable normalized residual, including a proof that an identified residual always has a rational observable functional.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen definitions say that the residual token carries finite candidate lists and define how to verify a listed candidate, but they neither specify an exhaustive compiler nor prove that one of the lists contains a passing candidate. Local response contrasts need not lift through an observed descendant or interacting district, and finite semialgebraic identifiability alone does not imply rational identifiability.
obligation.attempted: I checked the affine terminal-response route by row-space and null-space reduction and rechecked the supplied two-context contrast exactly. I also considered ordinary ID lifting and generic finite polynomial elimination. The first does not control arbitrary descendants and shared kernels; the second may return algebraic, rather than rational, functions and is expressly not the claimed structured causal compiler.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved normalization theorem reduces the question without enlarging the parameter image.  For a terminal binary response vector \(r\) with conditional observation and target maps \(O(r)=c+Wr\) and \(T(r)=c_*+hr\), a common response perturbation exists exactly when \(h\) is not in the row span of \(W\).  Indeed, if \(h=\gamma^{\mathsf T}W\), then \(Wd=0\) implies \(hd=0\).  Conversely, row reduction of \(W\), followed by reduction of the row \(h\), gives \(d\) in the null space of \(W\) with \(hd
e0\) whenever \(h\) is outside that row span.  If \(W\) and \(h\) are rational, this reduction gives rational \(d\).  If every coordinate of \(r\) is strictly between zero and one, the finitely many inequalities \(0<r_j+td_j<1\) contain a nonempty rational open interval about zero.  On that interval \(O(r+td)=O(r)\) and \(T(r+td)-T(r)=t hd
e0\) for \(t
e0\).  The worked execution verifies one such common contrast across both supported contexts.  This closes terminal affine residuals but not lifting through arbitrary interacting districts or the possibility of an identified nonrational residual.
